chunks: Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from Al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:
And do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress.
He said: It refers to a man who divorces, then when her term is about to expire, he takes her back, then divorces her again. He does that three times, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, forbade that.

key_terms.أَجَلُهَا: her term; the waiting period approaching its completion
key_terms.ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ: three times; repeated recurrence of the harmful practice
key_terms.رَاجَعَهَا: he takes her back; he revokes the divorce during the waiting period
key_terms.ضِرَارًا: harmfully; with the intent of causing injury or distress
key_terms.لِتَعْتَدُوا: so that you transgress; to commit wrongdoing beyond lawful limits
key_terms.يُطَلِّقُ: he divorces; initiates divorce against his wife

ai.seo_question: What does the verse 'And do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress' mean in the context of divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic prohibition against retaining a wife in a harmful manner during divorce proceedings. It refers to a man who repeatedly revokes the divorce near the end of the ʿiddah only to divorce again, using the process to cause harm. Allah forbade this abusive practice.
